abstracting everything away is an anti-pattern.

they reduce complexity by hiding everything from the user, which might be great for a consumer product, but it's the exact opposite of what you want in a tool for work.

people want to be able to both tweak and see the system.

you can do this in a way that's non-invasive, but they've gone the route of eliminating control and visibility entirely, which i think is a mistake for enterprise.

though its unclear if they are even focused on enterprise at all. everything about it is very consumer-y. coming from a team who knows how important enterprise is, i find it a bit puzzling.

if spacex/cursor wants a genuine claude code moment, they need to…

- keep the good parts of what they have in grok bot
- adapt it to be something enterprises will use
